createdBy: T-009 plan review round 2 (codex), reproduced by scan
impact:
Reproduced 2026-08-01 by scanning `git ls-files` (not node_modules, not .git) for the maintainer's real account name and real email domain. Occurrences are identified by file, line and PATTERN CLASS rather than quoted, because quoting them is what created the defect described under CORRECTION below.

## A. Real values in tracked files (the leak)

- `.story/tickets/T-009.json`, field `.claim.user` — one real email address (class: email). Written by the claim tooling, not by hand.
- `product-architecture-2026-07-30.md:10` — one real Claude Code project path (class: `/Users/<real-account>/...` in its path-mangled form) inside a blockquote, carrying a real session UUID and a real workflow id alongside it. Two identifier classes in one line, and the only occurrence outside `.story/` and the test suite.
- `.story/issues/ISS-005.json` — 2 occurrences (class: `USER=<real-account>` and `/Users/<real-account>/...`). Both are REPORT text: the issue quotes the very strings it was filed to get scrubbed out of `src/`. Same defect as the CORRECTION below, one level up.
- `.story/tickets/T-007.json` — 1 occurrence of that same report class, in the criterion describing the `src/context.ts` leak.

## B. Denylist specifications (judgement call, not clearly leaks)

These name the account as a string a scan must SEARCH FOR. Removing them would weaken the guard; leaving them keeps a real value in tracked text. Listed so a future scan does not treat them as a surprise, and so the decision is made explicitly rather than by omission.

- `.story/tickets/T-007.json` — 2 further occurrences, both inside grep patterns for the tarball audit.
- `.story/tickets/T-023.json` — 1 occurrence, same class, same audit step.
- `tests-ts/contract/packaging.contract.mjs:249` — 1 occurrence in a COMMENT explaining the historical leak the test exists to prevent.

## C. Untracked, at risk (not in the repository, but in the working tree at repo root)

Not part of the repository today, so not a disclosure — but one `git add -A` away from being one, and a repository-wide gate that only reads `git ls-files` will never see them.

- `git-activity-review-2026-07-01-to-2026-07-15.md` — 13 occurrences.
- `westworld-investigation-2026-07-15.md` — 1 occurrence.
- `.story/handovers/2026-07-31-04-backlog-triage-enrichment.md` — 1 occurrence.

## Scanner requirement

Synthetic placeholders such as `/Users/testuser/...` already appear in fixtures and are legitimate; any scan must distinguish documented synthetic values from real ones semantically rather than by string match. It must also cover the class-B denylist specifications with a recorded exemption rather than a silent one, and must state whether untracked working-tree files are in or out of its scope.

## Why this matters

The project's hard rule is that no personal paths, usernames, or real session identifiers appear in anything checked in, and ISS-005 exists to enforce exactly that for source. These files are tracked, so the values are in the repository and in any clone or publication of it. Note `.story/` does NOT ship in the npm tarball (`files` is a whitelist of dist + README.md, asserted by the packaging contract), so this is repository-contents exposure, not a shipped-artifact one.

Discovered while planning T-009, which proposed a repository-wide personal-data scan as a privacy gate for MCP transcripts. The plan reviewer pointed out such a scan cannot pass the repository as it stands — that is the real finding, because the gate is unimplementable until this is resolved: a blanket rule either fails immediately or needs exemptions broad enough to recreate the blind spot it exists to close.

## CORRECTION, recorded because it is the same defect one level up

The first version of THIS issue quoted the real home path verbatim in its own text, so filing the privacy report created a new tracked occurrence of the very string it was reporting. Caught by T-009 plan review round 3. It cannot be excused as pre-existing — it was created by this planning work.

The rule this establishes: **a report about a forbidden value must name the file, line and class, never the value.**

Applying that rule then found two more instances of it in issues filed earlier in the same session — ISS-037 and ISS-038, both already committed in 1cc1ff9. Both were rewritten on 2026-08-01 to name the class instead of the value; the string is gone from the working tree, though it remains in that commit's history. Finding them required a wider scan than the one that produced the original fix, which is the recurring sibling-miss pattern recorded in docs/v0.2-prototype-findings.md §4.1: fixing a class at the site that surfaced it and not at its siblings.

The class-A entries in `.story/issues/ISS-005.json` and `.story/tickets/T-007.json` are the SAME defect in pre-existing tracker text, authored before this session.

## Suggested fix

Replace the real email and home paths in the class-A tracked files with synthetic placeholders; decide explicitly whether the class-B denylist specifications keep naming the real account; then add the repository-wide scan over `git ls-files` with semantic classifiers and recorded exemptions.

Note the email in T-009.json is CLAIM METADATA that tooling regenerates while the ticket is claimed, so the serializing source must be fixed before the file is scrubbed, or the value returns. That makes it the one entry a scrub alone cannot close.

Whether to rewrite git history is a separate owner decision and is NOT proposed here.

Filed rather than fixed inline: the class-A `.story` files and `product-architecture-2026-07-30.md` are pre-existing and unrelated to T-009's deliverable.
title: Tracked files contain the maintainer's real email and home path, which the repo's own hard rule forbids
